The Akut Kirurgi Databasen tracks patient volumes and surgical intervention rates across multiple reporting periods. An analysis of the database's records from 2019-2020 through 2022-2023 reveals significant fluctuations in both the total patient population and the proportion of patients who underwent surgery [^src1]. 

When evaluating the total patient volume, the highest number of patients was recorded during the 2020-2021 period with 12,389 individuals, while the lowest volume occurred in 2021-2022 with 8,718 individuals [^src1]. The most recent period, 2022-2023, saw a total population of 10,013 patients [^src1]. 

The proportion of operated patients highlights a distinct outlier and a subsequent stabilizing trend. In 2019-2020, the surgical rate was at its absolute peak, with 59% of the 11,780 patients (6,932 individuals) undergoing operations [^src1]. This was followed by a dramatic drop in 2020-2021, where only 21% of the 12,389 patients (2,600 individuals) were operated on, marking the lowest surgical rate in the observed timeframe [^src1]. Following this trough, the surgical rate recovered, rising to 36% in 2021-2022 (3,134 out of 8,718 patients) and reaching 37% in 2022-2023 (3,697 out of 10,013 patients) [^src1]. Conversely, the non-operated patient group was highest in 2020-2021 with 9,789 individuals and lowest in 2019-2020 with 4,848 individuals [^src1]. No specific performance targets or thresholds are defined in this dataset to evaluate whether these rates met or missed institutional goals.

| 2021-2022 | 8.718 | 3.134 | 5.584 | 36 | % |
| 2020-2021 | 12.389 | 2.600 | 9.789 | 21 | % |
| 2019-2020 | 11.780 | 6.932 | 4.848 | 59 | % |

Entities: akut-kirurgi-databasen

Summary: Tabellen sammenligner antallet af patienter i Akut Kirurgi Databasen over fire år, og viser en stigning i andelen af opererede patienter fra 21 % i 2020-2021 til 37 % i 2022-2023, samtidig med at totalpopulationen falder fra 12.389 til 10.013.
